relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-add
relations.evidence: The server-add subcommand is used to add one or more servers to a cluster.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-add
relations.evidence: Note that the server to be added can not be specified using the http scheme since, in 7.1+, addition must occur over a secure connection.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-add
relations.evidence: The name of the group to add the server to. If this option is not specified then the server is added to the default group.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-server-add
relations.evidence: You may specify "default" for disk based indexes or `memopt` for memory optimized indexes.

notable_absence.finding: server-add.md lets an operator add nodes and change cluster topology - a materially privileged operation - yet states no RBAC role or permission requirement anywhere, matching the same absence already flagged on couchbase-cli.md's own landing page and on cluster-edit.md in this batch. The page does gate the ADDED server's own credentials (--server-add-username/--server-add-password) but never states what role the person RUNNING server-add must hold on the existing cluster.

cross_component_finding: Multiple concrete, checkable authorship-provenance artifacts on this single page. (1) The second EXAMPLE block uses flag names that do not exist anywhere in this command's own SYNOPSIS or OPTIONS: '--server-username Administrator --server-password password' instead of the documented '--server-add-username'/'--server-add-password'. (2) That same example also writes '--group-name --index-storage-setting memopt', i.e. --group-name with no value immediately followed by another flag - a broken, unexecutable example as printed. (3) The wrong flag names in (1) are not random - they are exactly the flag names its near-identical sibling couchbase-cli-server-readd.md uses for the semantically identical parameter (the credentials of the user with permission to modify the topology of the node being added). server-readd's own OPTIONS read: '--server-username <username> ... This flag specifies the username for a user who has the ability to modify the cluster topology of the node being added back' - i.e. server-add's broken example looks like it was copy-pasted from server-readd.md without updating the flag names to match server-add's own, differently-named options. This is precisely the failure mode this round's hypothesis predicted for near-identical siblings under lighter TW review. Separately: server-add.md's --services option documents an explicit 'manager-only' service value ('No other service can be used alongside the "manager-only" service because the server with this service specified will only act as a cluster manager and will not run any of the other functional services') that, in the CLI's own words, describes exactly the same resulting node shape the already-promoted server:arbiter-node concept describes ('a cluster node running NO services... Created implicitly: a node added or joined with no services selected becomes one'). No page states these are the same mechanism - server-add.md never uses the word 'arbiter', and frames it as an explicit service selection rather than an implicit consequence of selecting none - so per the no-silent-merge rule this is flagged as a finding rather than forced into a relation, but it reads like the CLI's own, differently-framed and differently-named documentation of the identical underlying feature.
cross_product_finding: Plainly none stated or implied on this page - server-add is a self-managed Server cluster-topology operation; Capella customers do not add nodes through this CLI surface.
